passages.passage: When a dramatic video about a local restaurant spread through our school chat groups, few students stopped to ask who had produced it or why it had been shared. The video seemed convincing, yet it had been (1) ______ changed to hide the moment when the owner explained the mistake. Before sharing such material, readers should (2) ______ the original source, compare it with an independent report, and ask whether a single detail has been used to make the larger (3) ______ seem more certain than it really is. Our news club invited a journalist to explain how titles may (4) ______ attention by making doubt sound like confidence, and she showed us a photo whose (5) ______ had been cut from the picture. The most (6) ______ report, she argued, is not one that hides doubt but one that states clearly what remains open, separates evidence from opinion, and tells readers when an important question still has no answer. Students who (7) ______ before sharing a claim again give themselves time to notice missing evidence, strong emotion and strange timing. It is also important to (8) ______ a false story openly when new evidence appears rather than defend an earlier post out of pride. In a crowded online (9) ______, speed can create confidence without understanding, and confidence then travels faster than facts. The club therefore suggested a simple (10) ______: no one may forward a serious claim until two independent sources have been checked. At first some students found the (11) ______ difficult, but they soon discovered that a brief delay improved conversation. After several weeks, the group became more (12) ______ about the material it shared and less eager to judge people by a single photo. Their experience suggests that careful judgment is not a single lesson but a habit built through repeated (13) ______ and honest conversation. When students accept that responsibility, a confusing feed becomes an (14) ______ to think rather than a reason to panic. The club now ends every meeting with one question: what evidence would change our (15) ______?

questions.stem: 选择第 1 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 视频被剪辑的目的是隐藏店主解释错误的片段，因此 deliberately 表示“故意地”，与 hide 的目的完全一致。accidentally 表示无意中，和有意隐藏相矛盾；generously 表示慷慨地，无法修饰这种剪辑行为。本题还排除了 gradually，因为 gradual 强调过程缓慢，而剪辑行为在这里有明确意图。

questions.stem: 选择第 2 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: verify the original source 表示核查材料的最初来源，是媒体素养中的固定表达。confirm 更常表示确认某个事实或说法，不能直接替代对 source 的核查动作；announce 表示公开宣布，replace 表示替换，二者都与来源核查无关。上下文要求读者在转发前采取核实动作，因此 verify 最准确。
questions.context_clue: verify 与 confirm 都能表示确认，但宾语是 source 时需要 verify。
questions.clue_argument: verify the source 表示核实来源；confirm 通常确认事实或说法。

questions.stem: 选择第 3 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: a larger account 表示对事件更完整、更宏大的叙述，与 single detail 形成“细节和整体叙事”的对照。report 通常指一份具体报告，和 larger 搭配时更像文件规模，而不是“整体叙述”；costume 和 melody 也不能表示信息如何被组织成完整故事。语境讨论的是叙事结构，因此 account 最合适。
knowledge_points: 名词：信息叙事与整体表述

questions.stem: 选择第 4 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: headlines attract attention 是自然搭配，表示标题通过制造确定性来吸引注意。collect attention 不是常用搭配；protect attention 和 divide attention 也不符合“标题吸引读者”的语境。句子强调媒体如何抓住注意力，因此 attract 最准确。
knowledge_points: 动词：注意力与媒体标题

questions.stem: 选择第 5 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 照片的 background 被裁掉后，画面的含义随之改变，这与后文 changing what viewers believed 形成直接因果。setting 虽然也指环境，但更强调地点背景的整体设定；caption 是文字说明，border 是边框，二者都不是被裁掉后改变事件理解的核心视觉背景。此处强调的是视觉信息被选择性删除，因此 background 最准确。
questions.context_clue: background 与 setting 都涉及环境，但图片中被裁掉的是画面背景。
questions.clue_argument: background 指画面背景；setting 更强调故事或事件发生的地点设定。

questions.stem: 选择第 6 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 可靠的报道不会隐藏不确定性，而会清楚说明哪些问题仍无答案，因此 reliable 与后文定义一致。expensive、familiar 和 colourful 描述的是价格、熟悉度或颜色，都不能体现报道在证据上的可信度。该句讨论的是真假与证据，不应选外观或成本形容词。

questions.stem: 选择第 7 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: pause before reposting 表示转发前先停一下，为检查证据留出时间，与后文的 notice missing evidence 相符。compete 表示竞争，escape 表示逃离，complain 表示抱怨，都不能表达“延迟转发以核查”的动作。本题通过 before 和 give themselves time 明确提示暂停。
knowledge_points: 动词：延迟转发与审慎判断

questions.stem: 选择第 8 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 当新证据出现时，应公开 correct a false story，也就是纠正此前的不实说法。repeat 会让错误继续传播；publish 和 support 都可能扩大错误影响，与 rather than defend 所要求的承认和修正相反。新证据出现后的责任是纠错，因此选 correct。

questions.stem: 选择第 9 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: a crowded online environment 表示拥挤的网络环境，是描述数字传播空间的自然搭配。instrument、ceremony 和 appetite 分别指工具、仪式和食欲，无法表示信息传播所处的环境。后文 speed 与 confidence travel faster 也明确指向网络传播空间。

questions.stem: 选择第 10 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 冒号后的 no one may forward ... 是对一条规则的完整说明，因此 a simple rule 是最准确的概括。request 只是一项请求，promise 是承诺，question 是问题，三者都不能表达“禁止未经核实转发”的规定。no one may 的强制性结构直接提示规则。

questions.stem: 选择第 11 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 前文要求等待两个独立来源核实后才能转发，这形成了 a requirement，学生起初觉得它 inconvenient 很自然。celebration 和 invitation 都与强制等待的规则无关；accident 表示事故，也不能表示一项要求。代词 the 指回前一句的 rule，因此 requirement 最连贯。

questions.stem: 选择第 12 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 学生更谨慎地对待分享材料，并与 less eager to judge 形成语义呼应，因此 cautious 最合适。generous 表示慷慨，curious 表示好奇，famous 表示著名，都不能体现减少草率判断的变化。about the material it shared 也明确指向对信息保持谨慎。

questions.stem: 选择第 13 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: repeated reflection and honest discussion 表示反复反思和诚实讨论，符合媒体素养需要长期养成的句意。practice 更偏向动作训练，argument 强调争执，praise 强调赞扬，都不能与下一分句的 honest discussion 形成“思考—交流”的互补。与 repeated 搭配时，reflection 最能体现习惯形成。

questions.stem: 选择第 14 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 空前是 an，且 opportunity 与 to think 构成“思考的机会”，与后半句 rather than a reason to panic 形成积极转折。possibility 前应使用 a，而且 a possibility to think 不如 opportunity 自然；obstacle 和 apology 更与这里的积极意义冲突。本题同时利用冠词和语义排除干扰项。
questions.context_clue: opportunity 与 possibility 语义接近，但空前冠词是 an。
questions.clue_argument: an opportunity 搭配正确；possibility 前应使用 a。

questions.stem: 选择第 15 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: what evidence would change our belief 表示什么证据会改变我们的信念，与全文关于核实和修正错误的主旨一致。plan 是具体安排，habit 是行为习惯，message 是传递内容，三者都不是由证据直接检验真假的观点。全文围绕判断与纠错展开，因此 belief 最合适。

passages.passage: When our town announced that cars would be (1) ______ from the street beside three schools during morning hours, some shop owners feared that customers would disappear. The town leaders replied that the change was only (2) ______: it would run for six months, gather clear information, and then face a public vote. Its aim was not to punish drivers but to give children safer (3) ______ to school, especially those who walked or cycled through heavy traffic every day. City workers (4) ______ residents, measured air quality, and allowed delivery firms to use the street before eight, while buses received a separate line. Volunteers (5) ______ crossings during the first weeks, helping younger students and reporting dangerous behaviour, and the early results surprised people who had doubted the plan because the number of cars fell (6) ______. A shop that had expected fewer customers reported a (7) ______ rise in sales of about four percent, which was welcome but far from dramatic. However, older residents who could not walk far found the new route (8) ______, so the town introduced a free electric bus and improved parking near the library. What matters in this debate is not whether every driver is pleased but whether the town can (9) ______ security, health, and fair use of public space. Officials promised to publish all traffic counts, accident reports, and shop sales instead of selecting only the figures that looked (10) ______. Researchers will (11) ______ the project until spring and compare it with three nearby towns, while students report their journey times and problems. If the final report shows real gains without serious harm, more families may (12) ______ their usual journeys and choose walking or cycling for short trips. The trial has not removed argument, but it has turned an argument about cars into a careful talk about how a town can (13) ______ different needs. What began as a local (14) ______ may become a lasting model, while any future (15) ______ will have to protect the routes used by residents nearby.

questions.stem: 选择第 1 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: be restricted from the street 表示车辆在特定时段被限制进入该街道，与 beside three schools 和 morning hours 的交通管理语境一致。limited 虽然也表示限制，但常用 limited to，和 from 搭配不自然；invited 表示被邀请，repaired 表示被修理，都无法描述车辆通行规则。介词 from 和公共道路管理语境共同确定 restricted。
knowledge_points: 动词：交通限制与介词搭配
questions.context_clue: restricted 与 limited 都表示限制，但介词是 from。
questions.clue_argument: restricted from 表示禁止进入；limited 通常与 to 搭配。

questions.stem: 选择第 2 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 后文说明该方案只运行六个月并随后投票，因此 temporary 表示“暂时的”，与固定试行期最吻合。accidental 表示偶然发生，不能说明方案有明确期限；ordinary 和 familiar 也不能体现“只实行六个月”的时间限制。此处核心是时长有限，temporary 最直接。

questions.stem: 选择第 3 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: safer paths to school 表示更安全的上下学路线，与 children who walked or cycled through heavy traffic 对应。crossings、signs 和 corners 虽然都与街道有关，却不能整体表示孩子从家到学校的路线。to school 前需要表示完整通行路径的名词，因此 paths 正确。

questions.stem: 选择第 4 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: City workers interviewed residents 表示工作人员采访居民，与后文他们又测量空气质量和安排送货形成完整的调研过程。observed 表示观察，虽然语法可行，但不如 interviewed 能引出居民意见；interrupted 和 instructed 分别表示打断和指示，语境不符。此处强调的是听取居民看法。

questions.stem: 选择第 5 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: volunteers monitored crossings 表示志愿者持续观察并管理路口，与 helping younger students and reporting dangerous behaviour 的任务相符。observed 只表示看见或观察，不包含维持秩序和持续管理；blocked 会阻止通行，cleaned 是清洁，都不能涵盖帮助和报告行为。后文的 reporting 明确提示持续观察。
knowledge_points: 动词：交通观察与志愿服务
questions.context_clue: monitored 与 observed 都涉及观察，但任务还包括管理和报告。
questions.clue_argument: monitored 强调持续监督；observed 只表示看到或观察。

questions.stem: 选择第 6 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: number of cars fell sharply 表示汽车数量大幅下降，与后文结果 surprised people who had doubted the plan 形成呼应。slightly 表示轻微下降，不足以产生强烈惊讶；briefly 描述持续时间，equally 描述相等程度。surprised 和 early results 共同提示下降幅度明显。

questions.stem: 选择第 7 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 后文 about four percent 和 far from dramatic 明确说明涨幅不大，因此 modest 表示“小幅的”最准确。sharp 表示急剧上升，与 far from dramatic 矛盾；frequent 描述发生频率而不是幅度，absent 表示不存在，也与 rise 冲突。上下文中的数字直接确定了答案。

questions.stem: 选择第 8 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: older residents who could not walk far 会认为新路线不方便，因此 inconvenient 与 could not walk far 直接对应。invisible、impolite 和 incomplete 分别表示不可见、不礼貌和不完整，都不能描述因行动距离增加产生的不便。后半句提供免费电动公交，也说明问题是不便。
knowledge_points: 形容词：无障碍与便利性

questions.stem: 选择第 9 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: balance security, health, and fair use 表示在安全、健康和公共空间公平使用之间取得平衡，正对应不同群体利益的冲突。relax security 与公共安全目标相反；announce 只表示宣布，divide 表示分割，都不能处理三项并列需求。三项目标之间的取舍提示需要 balance。

questions.stem: 选择第 10 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: figures that looked favourable 表示只挑选看起来有利的数据，与前文 publish all traffic counts 相对。positive 也能表示积极，但更泛化，不能突出“选择对自己有利的数字”；ordinary 和 missing 也不能体现选择性展示。instead of selecting only 明确指向原始数据可能带有偏向。
questions.context_clue: favourable 与 positive 都可表示有利或积极。
questions.clue_argument: favourable 强调对某一方有利，positive 更泛化，不能突出选择性偏向。

questions.stem: 选择第 11 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: follow the project until spring 表示持续跟踪项目进展，并与 compare it with three nearby towns 形成研究过程。replace 和 publish 是处理结果的后期动作，abandon 则表示停止跟踪，三者都不能与 until spring 构成持续研究。until spring 和 compare 是持续跟踪的直接线索。

questions.stem: 选择第 12 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: adjust their usual journeys 表示家庭调整日常出行方式，与 choose walking or cycling 的转变相符。rebuild 通常用于重建实体或关系，不能表示调整路线；announce 和 defend 分别表示宣布和辩护，也不能与 journeys 形成自然搭配。后文选择步行或骑车说明原方式需要调整，而不是完全消失。

questions.stem: 选择第 13 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: satisfy different needs 表示满足不同群体的需要，与前文居民、商店、老人和学生的多种利益对应。repeat 表示重复，admire 表示赞赏，replace 表示替代，都不能表示政策同时回应多种需要。different needs 是 satisfy 的常见搭配。

questions.stem: 选择第 14 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: a local experiment 表示一次地方试点，与 six months、public vote 和 trial 的含义完全一致。argument 表示争论，ceremony 表示仪式，warning 表示警告，都不能概括一项可被测试和调整的交通方案。该句总结变化可能成为长期模式，先导性质提示 experiment。

questions.stem: 选择第 15 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: future expansion 表示未来扩大该试点范围，与 routes used by residents nearby 可能受到影响相呼应。exception、entrance 和 celebration 都不能表示政策或项目规模扩大。while 引出的潜在影响说明这里讨论的是未来扩展。

passages.passage: ① ______ in shallow soil beside a new road, the young trees struggled through their first dry summer. Trees block direct sun from a surface, but they also cool the air through water lost from their leaves, so a green street works like a simple cooling system. Parks create cool islands ② ______ during summer afternoons, while lines of trees protect walkers from the strongest rays. City workers measure ③ ______ at different hours, because a covered side street may remain cooler than a wide road without cover. The council has also proposed that every new tree plan ④ ______ by an independent expert before planting begins. Only after several summers ⑤ ______ the difference between a newly planted row and a larger tree cover. The trees ⑥ ______ attract birds, reduce traffic noise, and make walking more comfortable. ⑦ ______, they should not be flooded; deep watering once a week is better than a little water daily. Researchers want to know ⑧ ______, so they compare electricity bills from buildings with different levels of cover. Since 2021, the city ⑨ ______ more than five hundred trees, and its map now includes every new planting. Students now use ⑩ ______ beside the oldest trees, where science lessons connect leaf temperature, soil water, and neighbourhood comfort. The project shows that effective city cooling depends less on the number of trees alone than on careful planting, patient care, and a plan that includes the people who use the street.

questions.stem: 选择第 ① 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 树已经被种在浅土中，之后才经历第一个干旱夏天，因此需要用完成被动非谓语 Having been planted 表示动作先于主句。Being planted 表示正在被种植；Having planted 的主动关系与 trees 不符；To be planted 表示将来目的，也不能交代先后关系。被动和完成两个意义缺一不可。

questions.stem: 选择第 ② 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: cool islands 表示较凉的区域，人们是在这个区域“里面”休息，因此 in which 与先行词和语义一致。for which 表示目的，with which 表示工具，by which 表示方式，都不能表达“在凉爽区域中休息”。本题需要同时判断介词和先行词的空间关系。

questions.stem: 选择第 ③ 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: measure 后需要名词性从句作宾语，what temperatures 表示“达到什么样的温度”，what 在从句中限定名词 temperatures。which 暗示已有范围，that 不能保留后面的名词中心语，how temperatures 搭配不完整。这里的核心是测量结果的数值范围。

questions.stem: 选择第 ④ 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: proposed that every plan be reviewed 使用虚拟语气，that 从句中的动词用原形 be，不随单复数或时态变化。is reviewed 和 was reviewed 都是陈述语气形式，to be reviewed 需要前面的 plan 作逻辑主语，却不能直接充当从句谓语。plan 与 review 还是被动关系，因此 be reviewed 正确。

questions.stem: 选择第 ⑤ 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: Only after several summers 位于句首时，主句要使用部分倒装，因此助动词 did 放到主语 residents 前。residents recognized 没有倒装；had residents recognized 表示过去完成，与主句时间不符；were residents recognized 变成被动，居民不会“被认出差异”。时间状语 only after 决定了 did 倒装。
knowledge_points: 倒装：Only after 部分倒装

questions.stem: 选择第 ⑥ 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 先行词 trees 是复数，定语从句的谓语要用复数 line，关系词在从句中作主语，因此 which line 正确。which lines 的主谓不一致；where 不能在从句中作主语；whose 表示所属关系，但 line the road 不是“其路线”的结构。主谓一致是本题的关键。

questions.stem: 选择第 ⑦ 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: 前句承认幼树需要水，后句强调不应淹水，二者构成让步关系，因此 Although 最合适。Because 会变成因果重复；Unless 和 If 都没有体现“需要水但不能过量”的让步对比。分号后的否定建议是选择让步连词的关键线索。

questions.stem: 选择第 ⑧ 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: want to know 后表示“是否”的不确定问题，需要 whether 引导名词性从句；后文比较不同遮阴程度的电费，说明研究者想知道遮阴是否降低用电。what 和 which 会错误地要求名词中心语，that 则把不确定问题变成已知事实。so they compare 进一步证明结果尚未确定。

questions.stem: 选择第 ⑨ 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: Since 2021 与 now includes every new planting 共同表示从过去持续到现在并产生当前结果，需要使用现在完成时 has planted。had planted 表示过去完成，缺少另一个过去参照点；will plant 表示将来，is planting 表示正在发生，都与 since 2021 的时间范围不符。时间标志和当前结果共同确定答案。

questions.stem: 选择第 ⑩ 空最合适的选项。
questions.explanation: outdoor 以元音音素开头，单数可数名词前需要不定冠词 an，表示“一个户外教室”；an outdoor classroom 与前文没有明确指代关系。a outdoor classroom 冠词形式错误，the 会产生不必要的特指，零冠词则缺少单数可数名词所需限定词。冠词和首次提及共同确定 an。

passages.passage:
When a community music group began holding open practice evenings in an old railway hall, its members expected only a few curious neighbours. They also thought a handful of families might wait quietly for the players to finish. Instead, people came with children, notebooks, walking sticks, and questions about instruments they had never tried closely before. The group had lost its usual concert audience during a long period of repairs at the town hall. The open evenings were first planned as a brief answer. They soon became the part of the week that players and residents valued most, because the hall let people listen without needing expert knowledge or costly tickets.

During a normal evening, the conductor explains why a passage is repeated, and a violin player shows how bow pressure changes the sound. Members of the audience are also invited to move closer when the music becomes quiet. These comments do not turn the event into a lecture; rather, they make the small decisions of a performance visible and give listeners a reason to care about details they might otherwise miss. One older resident said that she had attended concerts for decades but had never realised how much silent counting took place before a group began together.

A teenager who came only to finish a school project returned each week and later joined the youth singing group. This showed that access can lead to taking part when the first step is made easy. The third part of the evening is less formal on purpose: chairs are moved, visitors may ask short questions, and the group tries a new piece in front of everyone. This part matters because it changes the audience from judges of a finished product into witnesses of a process that is not yet fixed. Not every test succeeds, and the players sometimes stop after a few bars, laugh, and begin again; those moments make the art feel human rather than distant.

The town hall has now opened again, but the group has decided to keep the open evenings and make them a lasting part of its season. Its experience suggests that arts groups become stronger when they offer people more than a seat at the end of the work, inviting them instead into the questions, mistakes, and discoveries that give a performance meaning.

passages.passage:
On the first Saturday of every month, the community centre opens its main room to a repair club where neighbours bring damaged lamps, coats, loose chair legs, and small machines that have stopped working. No money changes hands, and no one is expected to know how to repair anything before arriving. Instead, volunteers sit beside visitors, explain each step, and invite the owner to hold the tool or test the switch.

The aim is not simply to rescue an object but to reduce waste while helping people understand how everyday products are built. Many visitors arrive believing that a small fault means the whole item must be replaced, and the first surprise is often how quickly a loose wire or worn belt can be found. A retired electrical worker who volunteers at the club says that the most useful tool is not a machine but a question: what changed just before the object stopped working? That question turns repair into a form of investigation and helps owners notice details they had ignored.

One student brought a desk lamp that had been left on a shelf for two years, and after replacing a cheap switch she began repairing bike lights for friends. The club also keeps a simple record of failed repairs, because some products are glued shut or use parts that may not be bought separately. These failures are displayed beside successful repairs, not hidden, so visitors can see that not every object can be saved and that design choices affect how long a product lasts. The student and the failed repair shelf show that learning comes from testing, observing, and admitting limits.

Local shops have responded in different ways: some donate spare parts, while others worry that free repairs reduce their income. The organisers reply that the club mainly handles simple faults and often sends complex jobs to professionals, so cooperation can replace doubt. After two years, the group estimates that it has kept more than eight hundred bags of material out of waste. More importantly, visitors leave with a changed habit: they are less likely to throw something away before asking whether it can be understood, opened, and repaired.

questions.stem: What question does the retired electrical worker consider most useful?

questions.evidence_sentence: A retired electrical worker who volunteers at the club says that the most useful tool is not a machine but a question: what changed just before the object stopped working?

passages.passage:
In many families, practical knowledge passes silently from one generation to the next, yet it is often lost when young people move to cities, live alone, or depend on professional services for every small problem. An older relative may know how to make a knife sharp, repair damaged clothing, or judge when bread has grown, but such skills often remain unnoticed until the person who holds them is no longer nearby. When the older person stops being able to demonstrate a task, the gap may feel like a sudden loss rather than a gradual absence of memory. Digital videos offer useful access to information, and they can show a procedure from several angles, but information alone does not create judgment. (1) ______

A family kitchen or work area can become a place for teaching when adults explain not only what to do but also how to notice when something is going wrong. A young person who cooks with an aunt learns to listen for the change in sound as water begins to boil and to feel when dough has been pressed enough, and those signals are difficult to describe without practice. (2) ______

The process also changes the relationship between generations. Young people are often seen as learners, while older relatives are seen as providers of advice; when they complete a practical task together, both roles become more equal and more flexible. (3) ______

Specific traditions matter as well because they carry memory and identity, not just technique. (4) ______ Teaching can fail when it becomes a test or a performance, so the atmosphere should leave room for mistakes, questions, and repeated attempts. A family that laughs at a badly shaped dumpling is more likely to continue the lesson than one that treats every error as evidence of carelessness. (5) ______

The goal is not to preserve every old method exactly as it was once used. It is to give young people enough practical confidence to solve problems, appreciate the knowledge around them, and pass something useful forward when their own turn comes.

questions.stem: 选择最适合第 (1) 空的句子。
options: Over time, repeated practice turns a clumsy action into a dependable habit.

However, this shared work also gives family members something to discuss when conversation becomes difficult.
